claim: Amazon EventBridge provides real-time access to changes in data in AWS services, your own applications, and software as a service (SaaS) applications without writing code.
question: What is Amazon EventBridge?

values.display: real-time access to changes in data

evidence.quote: Amazon EventBridge is a service that provides real-time access to changes in data in AWS services, your own applications, and software as a service (SaaS) applications without writing code.

claim: You can generate custom application-level events and publish them to EventBridge through the service's API operations.
question: Can I publish my own events to EventBridge?

evidence.quote: Yes. You can generate custom application-level events and publish them to EventBridge through the service’s API operations.

claim: A rule matches incoming events for a given event bus and routes them to targets for processing.
question: How do I filter which events are delivered to a target?

values.display: matches incoming events for a given event bus

evidence.quote: A rule matches incoming events for a given event bus and routes them to targets for processing.

claim: A single rule can route to multiple targets, all of which are processed in parallel.
question: Can one EventBridge rule send an event to more than one target?

evidence.quote: A single rule can route to multiple targets, all of which are processed in parallel.

claim: A rule can customize an event before it is sent to the target, by passing only certain parts or by overwriting it with a constant.
question: Can an EventBridge rule change an event before it reaches the target?

values.display: customize an event before it is sent to the target

evidence.quote: A rule can customize an event before it is sent to the target, by passing only certain parts or by overwriting it with a constant.

claim: Amazon EventBridge is recommended when you want to build an application that reacts to events from your own applications, SaaS applications, and AWS services.
question: When should I use EventBridge and when should I use SNS?

values.display: reacts to events from your own applications

evidence.quote: Amazon EventBridge is recommended when you want to build an application that reacts to events from your own applications, SaaS applications, and AWS services.

claim: EventBridge is the only event-based service that integrates directly with third-party SaaS partners.
question: Which event-based service integrates directly with third-party SaaS partners?

evidence.quote: EventBridge is the only event-based service that integrates directly with third-party SaaS partners.

claim: EventBridge uses a defined JSON-based structure for events, and rules are applied across the entire event body to select events to forward to a target.
question: How does EventBridge select events to forward to a target?

values.display: applied across the entire event body

evidence.quote: EventBridge uses a defined JSON-based structure for events, and helps you create rules that are applied across the entire event body to select events to forward to a target.

claim: Amazon SNS is recommended for applications that need high fan out, which means thousands or millions of endpoints.
question: When should I use EventBridge and when should I use SNS?

evidence.quote: Amazon SNS is recommended for applications that need high fan out (thousands or millions of endpoints).

claim: A common pattern is to use SNS as a target for an EventBridge rule: the rule filters the events you need and SNS fans them out to multiple endpoints.
question: How do customers combine EventBridge rules and SNS?

values.display: use SNS as a target for their rule

evidence.quote: A common pattern that we see is that customers use SNS as a target for their rule to filter the events that they need and fan out to multiple endpoints.

claim: SNS messages are unstructured and can be in any format. SNS forwards messages to six different types of targets: Lambda, SQS, HTTP/S endpoints, SMS, mobile push, and email.
question: What formats and targets does SNS support compared with EventBridge?

values.display: unstructured and can be in any format

evidence.quote: Messages are unstructured and can be in any format. SNS supports forwarding messages to six different types of targets, including Lambda, SQS, HTTP/S endpoints, SMS, mobile push, and email.

claim: Amazon SNS typical latency is under 30 milliseconds.
question: What is the typical latency of Amazon SNS?

evidence.quote: Amazon SNS typical latency is under 30 milliseconds.

claim: Event Replay lets you reprocess past events back to an event bus or a specific EventBridge rule.
question: What is EventBridge Archive and Replay Events?

evidence.quote: Event Replay is a new feature for EventBridge that helps you reprocess past events back to an event bus or a specific EventBridge rule.

claim: Event Replay helps developers debug applications, extend them by hydrating targets with historic events, and recover from errors.
question: Why would I use EventBridge Replay?

values.display: extend them by hydrating targets with historic events

evidence.quote: This feature helps developers debug their applications more easily, extend them by hydrating targets with historic events, and recover from errors.

claim: API destinations help developers send events back to any on-premises or SaaS application, with control over throughput and authentication.
question: What is EventBridge API Destinations?

evidence.quote: API Destinations helps developers send events back to any on-premises or SaaS applications with the ability to control throughput and authentication.

claim: Each API destination uses a Connection that defines the authorization method and credentials. Creating a connection creates a secret in AWS Secrets Manager to store the authorization information securely.
question: What is a Connection for an API destination?

evidence.quote: Each API destination uses a Connection that defines the authorization method and credentials to use to connect to the HTTP endpoint. When you configure the authorization settings and create a connection, it creates a secret on AWS Secrets Manager to store the authorization information securely.

claim: For an API destination you can optionally define the invocation rate limit, which is the maximum number of invocations per second to send to the endpoint.
question: Can I limit how fast EventBridge calls an API destination?

values.display: maximum number of invocations per second

evidence.quote: You can also optionally define the invocation rate limit, which is the maximum number of invocations per second to send to the API destination endpoint.

claim: The typical latency between sending and receiving an event in EventBridge is about half a second, and it can vary.
question: What is the latency that I can expect between sending and receiving an event?

evidence.quote: Typical latency is about half a second. Note that this can vary.

claim: Default EventBridge quotas can be increased to process hundreds of thousands of events per second.
question: What throughput can I expect from EventBridge?

values.display: hundreds of thousands of events per second
Default EventBridge quotas can be increased

evidence.quote: Default EventBridge quotas can be increased to process hundreds of thousands of events per second.

claim: AWS will use commercially reasonable efforts to make EventBridge available with a Monthly Uptime Percentage for each AWS Region, during any monthly billing cycle, of at least 99.99%.
question: Does EventBridge have a Service Level Agreement?

evidence.quote: AWS will use commercially reasonable efforts to make EventBridge available with a Monthly Uptime Percentage for each AWS Region, during any monthly billing cycle, of at least 99.99%.

claim: You can tag EventBridge rules and event buses.
question: Does EventBridge support resource tagging?

evidence.quote: Yes, you can tag rules and event buses.

claim: A target can send events to another account. The target can be the default event bus or any other event bus in that account. These are called cross-account events.
question: Can I have a target that sends events to another account?

values.display: default event bus or any other event bus in another account

evidence.quote: Yes. These are called cross-account events, and you can have a target that is either the default event bus or any other event bus in another account.

claim: Cross-account events can centralize events from multiple accounts into a single event bus to monitor and audit them, and to keep data in sync between accounts.
question: Why would I send events to another account?

evidence.quote: This can be used to centralize events from multiple accounts into a single event bus to more easily monitor and audit your events, as well as to keep data in sync between accounts.
